text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.1% today as oil prices climbed sharply following escalating U.S.-Iran tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude topped $101 per barrel—its highest level since May—after reports that the U.S. destroyed Iranian oil tankers, raising concerns that the conflict could disrupt oil supply flows from the Persian Gulf. As an oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices move higher, since the company sells oil at those elevated prices.

The stock's 3.6% gain over the past two weeks reflects an even broader rally tied to these geopolitical risks. Oil has climbed steadily as the U.S.-Iran conflict has escalated, and investors are pricing in the likelihood that energy prices will remain elevated through the midterm elections, limiting the downside relief that might normally come from seasonal demand patterns.
